title: The Curfew Bell
author: thAImaturgy examples
summary: A market town welcomes visitors by day, but a tolling bell empties its streets at dusk — and something moves once the watch locks the gates.
context: A short investigation for a party of 1st-2nd level. It shows how one location can be run as two scenes: the same square, bustling by day and deserted under curfew. Use it as a template for phase-based adventures.
background: The night watch isn't protecting the town from the dark — it is covering for the smugglers who use the empty streets after curfew. The watch-captain rings the bell early on nights a shipment moves.
introduction: The party arrives in Graystone at midday, hired by a worried merchant whose courier vanished after curfew three nights ago. They have until dusk to look around; once the bell tolls, no one is supposed to be on the streets.
conclusion: The party can expose the watch-captain's smuggling ring (confront him during the curfew run), quietly recover the missing courier, or be run out of town. Any ending resolves what the bell really signals.
hooks: A merchant hires the party to find a courier who vanished after curfew.
One of the party recognizes the courier as an old friend.
The town pays unusually well for 'discreet' visitors who don't ask about the bell.

zones.name: Graystone
zones.overview: A walled market town built around a central square and its bell tower.

rooms.name: Market Square
rooms.read_aloud: Cobblestones ring with footsteps and haggling; the bell tower throws a long shadow across the stalls.
rooms.dm_notes: By day this is the hub. The vanished courier was last seen buying bread here.

exits.description: The Broken Tankard fronts the square.

rooms.name: The Broken Tankard
rooms.read_aloud: Low beams, spilled ale, and a hearth that never quite warms the room.
rooms.dm_notes: Neutral ground. The tavernkeeper knows the bell rings early on 'delivery' nights but fears the watch.

npcs.name: Elenya
npcs.appearance: A sharp-eyed baker with flour on her sleeves.
npcs.personality: Friendly but guarded once the sun starts to set.
npcs.motivations: Keep her stall and stay off the watch's bad side.
knowledge: Saw the courier the day he vanished
The bell has been ringing earlier than it used to

npcs.name: Captain Vorr
npcs.appearance: Broad-shouldered, immaculate uniform, a key ring that never leaves his belt.
npcs.personality: Courteous by day, coldly authoritative after the bell.
npcs.motivations: Move the shipments and keep the streets empty and quiet.
npcs.secrets: He rings the curfew bell early on nights a smuggling shipment moves.

events.name: The Bell Tolls
events.trigger: Dusk falls, or the party lingers too long in the open.
events.read_aloud: A deep bronze note rolls across the rooftops. Doors slam. Within minutes the square is empty.
events.dm_notes: Switch to the 'curfew' scene when this fires (set_scene curfew).

scenes.name: Before the Bell
scenes.description: Daytime investigation. The town is open and talkative; the party can gather leads before dusk.

rooms.present: packed with stalls and townsfolk; safe to ask questions

next.when: the curfew bell tolls at dusk (event the-bell), or the party is caught outside after dark

scenes.name: After the Bell
scenes.description: The streets are locked down. Being seen draws the watch; this is when the smuggling run happens.
scenes.read_aloud: The last echo of the bell fades. The town holds its breath behind shuttered windows.

rooms.read_aloud: Empty cobblestones gleam under the watch's lanterns. Bootsteps echo in the dark.
rooms.present: deserted; watch patrols; being seen is dangerous
shuttered and dark; the door is barred from inside
